take_homes: Split into several agents only for different access, different dialect or different stance. Otherwise write one good prompt.
A framework such as Rumelt's kernel makes the synthesizer pick one diagnosis instead of averaging three views. Better wording does not do that.
The failures happen at the handoffs between agents, and the audit checks the process, not whether the briefing is true.

monday.move: Run the three-retriever setup on the pricing pilot: wiki, docs and internet into files, then curate. I'll tell the synthesizer to flag where my sources disagree, and I'll look at the churn article first.
monday.who: Me first. Then one person from my team takes over the memory folder.
monday.stop_condition: The synthesis names a diagnosis I can defend to the CFO, or I find two sources conflicting and the curator has dropped one.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files and CLAUDE.md. Everyone keeps their own copy, and the module does not solve that.

misconception.why: The framework, not the prompt wording, changed how the synthesizer behaved. The split-or-not decision and the handoffs also mattered more than how clever any single prompt was. I still think prompts matter, but they are not the main thing now.

one_line: Good on when not to split agents and on where the handoffs break. It repeats 'use one agent' too often, and it doesn't say how a team shares the files.
